_comment: SKILL BLUEPRINT — output of the Spec agent, input to the Generator agent.
subject: math
cluster: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions
description: Students choose and build a sinusoidal model $f(x)=a\sin(b(x-h))+k$ (or the cosine form $f(x)=a\cos(b(x-h))+k$) for periodic real-world phenomena. They translate a specified amplitude, frequency or period, and midline into the parameters $a$, $b$, $k$, and a phase shift $h$, then use the model to evaluate, interpret, and solve. The student must connect each transformation parameter to its physical meaning: amplitude $=|a|$ (half the peak-to-trough distance), midline $y=k$ (the average/rest value), period $T=\frac{2\pi}{|b|}$ (or $\frac{1}{|b|}$ when $b$ is a frequency in cycles), frequency $=\frac{1}{T}$, and the phase shift $h$ that aligns the curve with a given starting feature (max, min, or midline crossing).
subSkills: Identify amplitude, midline, period, and frequency from a verbal description, a graph, or a data table
Convert between period and frequency, and compute $b$ from a period via $b=\frac{2\pi}{T}$
Choose between a sine and a cosine model based on the given starting feature (max/min vs. midline crossing) to minimize or set the phase shift
Assemble the parameters into $a\sin(b(x-h))+k$ or $a\cos(b(x-h))+k$ with correct signs
Determine the phase shift $h$ that places a known feature (peak, trough, or midline crossing) at a given input value
Evaluate the model at a given input and interpret the output in context (with units)
Solve the model for the input(s) that produce a target output over one period (read from a graph or by inverse reasoning)
Interpret amplitude, midline, period, and frequency back into the real-world quantity they represent

problemArchetypes.name: Build the equation from stated amplitude, midline, and period
problemArchetypes.example: Write a sine function with amplitude $3$, midline $y=5$, and period $4\pi$ that passes through its midline going upward at $x=0$. Answer: $f(x)=3\sin\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}x\right)+5$.

problemArchetypes.name: Frequency-to-parameter conversion
problemArchetypes.example: A wave completes $4$ cycles per second with amplitude $2$ about the line $y=0$. Write $h(t)=2\sin(8\pi t)$, since $b=2\pi f=2\pi\cdot 4=8\pi$.

problemArchetypes.name: Choose sine vs. cosine from the starting feature
problemArchetypes.example: A Ferris wheel rider starts at the lowest point ($2$ m) and the wheel peaks at $30$ m every $20$ s. Model the height: $H(t)=-14\cos\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{10}t\right)+16$, using $-\cos$ because the motion starts at a minimum.

problemArchetypes.name: Determine the phase shift to align a feature
problemArchetypes.example: Daylight peaks at $14.5$ h on day $172$ and the midline is $12$ h with period $365$. Write $D(t)=2.5\sin\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{365}(t-81.25)\right)+12$, choosing $h$ so the maximum lands at $t=172$.

problemArchetypes.name: Evaluate the model and interpret in context
problemArchetypes.example: For $T(t)=15\cos\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{6}(t-3)\right)+60$ (temperature in $^{\circ}$F, $t$ in hours after midnight), find $T(9)$ and state what it means. Answer: $T(9)=60^{\circ}$F, the daily average, reached $6$ hours after the $3$ a.m. low passes through midline.

problemArchetypes.name: Solve for inputs that give a target output
problemArchetypes.example: Given the tide model $h(t)=4\sin\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{6}t\right)+7$ (feet, $t$ in hours), find the first two times $t\ge 0$ when the tide is $9$ ft. Answer: $t=1$ and $t=5$ hours.

difficultyRubric._comment: A single ramped worksheet of 15 items runs Easy (items 1-5) to Medium (6-11) to Hard (12-15). If split: tier1 = Easy to Medium (read/convert/assemble parameters, no phase shift), tier2 = Medium to Hard (phase shift, interpretation, solving). Difficulty scales with the number of parameters that must be derived rather than read, whether a phase shift is required, and whether the student must also interpret or solve.

Easy.description: Amplitude, midline, and period (or $b$) are stated directly and only need to be placed into the standard form. No phase shift (curve starts at a midline crossing going up for sine, or at a max for cosine). One- or two-step.
constraints: Amplitude, midline, and period given explicitly in words
$b$ is a clean value, $T$ a simple multiple or fraction of $\pi$ (e.g. $2\pi$, $\pi$, $4\pi$, $\frac{\pi}{3}$)
Task is to write the equation OR identify one feature from a given equation

Medium.description: At least one parameter must be derived: compute $b$ from a period, or get amplitude and midline from a stated max and min via $a=\frac{\text{max}-\text{min}}{2}$ and $k=\frac{\text{max}+\text{min}}{2}$, or convert a frequency to $b$. May choose sine vs. cosine based on the starting feature. Phase shift is $0$ or a simple value.
constraints: Amplitude and/or midline derived from a given maximum and minimum
$b$ derived from a period or from a frequency in cycles per unit
Student selects sine or cosine (and sign of $a$) from the described start
Phase shift either $0$ or a single clean value
May ask for one evaluation of the finished model

Hard.description: Multi-step real-world model where the student must extract every parameter from context, determine a non-trivial phase shift to align a stated peak/trough/crossing at a given input, and then either evaluate, interpret, or solve the model for target outputs over one period.
constraints: All four features (amplitude, midline, period/frequency, phase reference) buried in a context paragraph
Requires a non-zero phase shift $h$ computed from a stated time of max or min
Follow-up requires evaluating in context with units OR solving for input value(s) yielding a target output
May require comparing two models or justifying the sine-vs-cosine choice

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student uses the period directly as $b$ instead of $b=\frac{2\pi}{T}$
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For period $4\pi$ writes $f(x)=3\sin(4\pi x)+5$ instead of $f(x)=3\sin\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}x\right)+5$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student inverts the period-frequency relationship, taking $b=\frac{T}{2\pi}$
Student takes amplitude as the full peak-to-trough distance instead of half of it
commonMisconceptions.distractor: With max $30$ and min $2$ uses $a=28$ instead of $a=\frac{30-2}{2}=14$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student computes the midline as the maximum (or as $0$) rather than the average of max and min
commonMisconceptions.distractor: With max $30$ and min $2$ uses $k=30$ (or $k=0$) instead of $k=\frac{30+2}{2}=16$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student keeps $+\cos$ when the motion starts at a minimum, ignoring the needed reflection
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Models a ride starting at the lowest point as $14\cos\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{10}t\right)+16$ instead of $-14\cos\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{10}t\right)+16$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student writes the phase shift with the wrong sign, using $(x+h)$ for a rightward shift
commonMisconceptions.distractor: To shift the peak to $t=172$ writes $\sin\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{365}(t+81.25)\right)$ instead of $(t-81.25)$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student confuses frequency with period, plugging the frequency in where the period belongs
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $4$ cycles per second uses $b=\frac{2\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}$ instead of $b=2\pi\cdot4=8\pi$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student adds the midline to the amplitude argument or otherwise mislocates $k$

_comment_itemCounts: Standard uses a single ramped worksheet (Easy->Hard across 15 items). lesson 5 worked examples + 5 practice, quiz 8 multiple-choice.
